symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A process-global resource mutated by tests in more than one module is serialized by ONE mutex; every test that touches it contends on that mutex.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: The frozen base path of a linear computes identically whether or not that linear happens to be a LoRA target; a configured backbone_dtype means the same thing at every site.
symptom_spec.observable: MaybeLoraLinear::Frozen casts the input DOWN to the weight dtype and runs the matmul in the backbone dtype (wrapper.rs:31-38), while LoraLinear::forward allocates a fresh full-size F32 copy of the frozen weight on EVERY forward and runs the base matmul in F32 (lora_linear.rs:239-255). With lora_b initialised to zeros the LoRA delta is exactly 0, so both arms must be bit-identical for the same input at a reduced dtype - and are not. Consequence: backbone_dtype=bf16/f16 is inert on exactly the linears a LoRA run targets (with target_modules covering Wqkv/Wo/Wi that is every ModernBERT linear), buys no compute saving, and costs a per-forward full-weight materialisation.
symptom_spec.control: Zero-delta equality between the two arms at a reduced dtype, gated non-vacuously: assert lora_b.abs().sum()==0 before comparing (else a non-zero delta is mistaken for a dtype difference), require both outputs finite by a finite-COUNT check rather than any comparison bound (a NaN makes both `diff<eps` and `diff>eps` false), require both non-constant (max-min>0) so a zeroed matmul cannot pass, and keep an F32 positive control that must pass today - proving the harness discriminates dtype rather than reporting inequality everywhere.

which_gate_missed: no gate - no test compares the Frozen and Lora arms against each other at any dtype, and the reduced-dtype fine-tune path has no coverage at all.
evidence_ref: crates/jammi-lora/src/lora_linear.rs@9ad1131:239-255 vs crates/jammi-lora/src/wrapper.rs@9ad1131:26-38. Reported as GH #345 with a different (incorrect) root cause.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A per-element dropout mask on a device-resident activation is produced on that device; it does not round-trip through the host, and it does not pin host-sized buffers in device memory for the backward pass.
symptom_spec.observable: LoraLinear::forward draws the mask with a single-threaded host scalar RNG loop over x.elem_count() (seeded.rs:127-135) and copies it device-ward via Tensor::from_vec on EVERY training forward (lora_linear.rs:278-284). For a ModernBERT-large-class encoder at batch 16 / seq 128 that is 0.98G host RNG draws and 3.92 GB of H2D per optimizer step (measured 0.31 s/step of pure host RNG on a fast desktop core, GPU idle throughout); at the shipped default max_seq_length=512 it is 1.96G draws and 7.84 GB. Because the mask is an operand of a mul whose other operand requires grad, every mask is additionally retained in device memory through backward - so the same quantity is a direct OOM contributor. Invisible to CPU-only tests, where the copy is free.
symptom_spec.control: Assert the per-forward host allocation is not proportional to batch*seq*in_features, and that mask residency does not scale with the number of LoRA sites on the tape. Pair with a determinism control: the mask stream must remain a pure function of (seed, qualified param name, position) so the fix cannot buy throughput by weakening reproducibility.

which_gate_missed: no gate - the hermetic suite is CPU-only, where a host-to-device copy has no cost and no distinct memory residency, so the entire failure mode is unobservable by construction.
evidence_ref: crates/jammi-lora/src/seeded.rs@9ad1131:127-135, crates/jammi-lora/src/lora_linear.rs@9ad1131:278-284. Surfaced while triaging GH #345, which attributes the slowdown to backbone_dtype instead.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: An encoder either honours every architecture field it accepts from a checkpoint's config, or refuses the checkpoint at load with a typed error naming the field it cannot honour. It never accepts a config it silently does not implement.
symptom_spec.observable: ModernBertConfig deserializes local_attention, local_rope_theta and global_attn_every_n_layers (modernbert.rs:83-88) and no forward or builder path reads them again: every layer builds its RoPE table from global_rope_theta (modernbert.rs:567-572) and attention adds only the padding mask (modernbert.rs:206-214). For any checkpoint with global_attn_every_n_layers != 1 - which includes the ModernBERT-large family at 3 - two of every three layers compute full global attention with the wrong RoPE base, i.e. a different function than the checkpoint specifies, with no error and no warning. The port's own doc comment declares its valid domain as global_attn_every_n_layers == 1 (modernbert.rs:63-70) and nothing enforces it.
symptom_spec.control: Causal-isolation on a local layer using a fixture that can express the symptom (multi-layer, global_attn_every_n_layers=3, window narrower than the sequence, no padding so the additive pad mask cannot be confused for the band): perturbing a token outside the window must leave an in-window position's local-layer state unchanged. Non-vacuous only with three controls in the same test - an in-window position MUST change (proves the perturbation propagates), the same position on a GLOBAL layer MUST change (proves the band is selective, not a broken forward), and both states asserted finite by a finite-COUNT check, since a -inf mask row that softmaxes to NaN passes any comparison-based 'unchanged' assertion.

which_gate_missed: no gate - every ModernBERT fixture in-tree is num_hidden_layers=1 / global_attn_every_n_layers=1, so layer 0 is global under both semantics and no fixture can express the divergence. The coverage hole and the defect share a root: the fixture set was built from the port's assumed domain.
evidence_ref: crates/jammi-encoders/src/modernbert.rs@9ad1131:83-88, :206-214, :567-572; blind fixtures at tests/fixtures/tiny_modernbert/config.json and cookbook/fixtures/tiny_modernbert_{classifier,ner}/config.json. Documented in GH #350, which proposes no change.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A metric that was never measured never drives checkpoint selection, early stopping, or a reported result. An empty measurement domain is refused, not scored.
symptom_spec.observable: evaluate() returns Ok(0.0) for an empty validation loader (trainer.rs:1627-1629). Under the DEFAULT early_stopping_metric=ValLoss this makes monitor_loss 0.0 every epoch: epoch 0 wins 0.0 < f64::MAX and writes checkpoint_best (trainer.rs:391, :586-589), every later epoch fails 0.0 < 0.0 and increments patience (:591-592), the loop breaks at patience+1 epochs, the epoch-0 checkpoint is reloaded as the PUBLISHED adapter (:625-628), and final_loss is reported as 0.0 (:657, :667). So a run silently ships an essentially untrained adapter and reports a perfect loss. Reachable two ways: explicit validation_fraction=0.0, and - not reported in the issue - the DEFAULT validation_fraction=0.1 on any dataset where round(N*0.1)==0, i.e. fewer than 5 rows.
symptom_spec.control: Assert the run completes its full epoch horizon, that the returned adapter is NOT bit-equal to the end-of-epoch-0 weights across ALL trainable params (exact equality, not a norm, so a partial restore cannot pass), and that final_loss is finite AND strictly positive - a bare `!= 0.0` is vacuous against NaN, which also silently satisfies `monitor < best` never firing, the same collapse in another mask. Positive control in the same test: the identical run with a non-empty validation split must train the full horizon and return a finite decreasing monitored loss.

which_gate_missed: no gate - validate() range-checks validation_fraction in [0.0,1.0) (fine_tune.rs:441-450) with no cross-field rule against ValLoss, and no test runs the trainer with an empty validation split.
evidence_ref: crates/jammi-ai/src/fine_tune/trainer.rs@9ad1131:1627-1629, :391, :586-592, :625-628, :657, :667; crates/jammi-ai/src/fine_tune/data.rs@9ad1131:465. Reported as GH #347, whose FIRST stated root cause is refuted (proto3 explicit presence already carries a set 0.0).

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: An operator that cannot participate in backward fails loudly when a gradient is required through it; it never silently returns a zero/absent gradient that reads as successful training.
symptom_spec.observable: candle's apply_op1_no_bwd constructs its result with BackpropOp::none() (candle-core custom_op.rs:156-159), so backward through such a tensor does not raise BackwardNotSupported - it stops traversing. Two operators the engine reaches for take this path: candle_nn::ops::softmax_last_dim (candle-nn ops.rs:437-439), already called at jammi-encoders/src/htsat_audio.rs:632, jammi-encoders/src/clip_text.rs:150 and jammi-ai/src/model/backend/open_clip_vit.rs:169; and QMatMul (candle-core quantized/mod.rs:1023), the natural entry point for quantized fine-tuning. Any trainable parameter placed upstream of one of these receives no gradient while the loss still decreases plausibly from the parameters that remain connected.
symptom_spec.control: A gradient-reachability assertion rather than a loss-decreases assertion: for every trainable Var, require a non-None, non-zero gradient after one backward on a non-degenerate batch. A test that only checks the loss went down cannot distinguish a partially-connected graph from a fully-connected one.

which_gate_missed: no gate - nothing asserts that every registered trainable Var actually receives a gradient. The three current call sites are correct only incidentally: neither the CLIP nor the HTSAT tower is LoRA-wrapped, so the truncation sits upstream of every Var.

notes.text: Research on 2026-08-23 confirmed the mechanism is unchanged in candle 0.11: apply_op1_no_bwd still constructs BackpropOp::none() (candle-core custom_op.rs:156-159), and a user CustomOp bwd() returning Ok(None) is also silently dropped (no gradient, no error) - same truncation class, a distinct call site. No upstream fix has landed. Tracked upstream issues: huggingface/candle#2168 (RmsNorm, opened 2024, still open), #2977 / #3011 (LayerNorm), #3568 (rope), #3569 (softmax_last_dim, re-verified against main HEAD 2026-05-28). Candidate fix PRs #3526, #3612, #3613, #3724 are all open/unmerged. NEW third named entry point for this row's operator list: candle_nn::ops::sdpa (candle-nn src/ops.rs ~1317) is implemented via apply_op3_no_bwd with no composed (slow) fallback twin - add it alongside softmax_last_dim and QMatMul as a silent-backward-truncation site. Proposed general mitigation surfaced in the #2168 thread: dispatch on Tensor::track_op() (candle-core tensor.rs:592, is_variable || op.is_some()) - take the fused/no-bwd kernel only when track_op() is false, and fall back to the composed/differentiable path when true. Row status stays open pending an upstream fix landing.

Fix landed on fix/esc-037-attention-softmax-backward (tip 8f12570). All three softmax_last_dim call sites named in this row now route training through the composed differentiable softmax (jammi_encoders::attention::attention_softmax) instead of the no-bwd fused kernel. TWO further homes of this class were found and fixed in the same branch: (1) candle_nn::LayerNorm::forward (candle-nn 0.11 layer_norm.rs:117-120 routes through ops::layer_norm = apply_op3_no_bwd, ops.rs:932-944) at every norm of CLIP-text, HTSAT, and OpenCLIP-vision -- these now use the house gated LayerNorm instead; (2) HTSAT mel_conv2d's non-dividing Tensor::unfold, whose backward candle registers as a plain Op::Reshape (tensor.rs:2931-2969, backprop.rs:602-606) that requires equal element counts -- fixed by narrowing to the largest divisible prefix before unfolding. CONTROL WORDING CORRECTION: this row's stated control, 'non-None, non-zero gradient for every trainable Var,' is INSUFFICIENT for a fused projection -- through the P.V matmul, the V slice of a fused in_proj_weight receives a nonzero gradient even when the softmax truncates upstream (measured at base: Q-slice grad-norm 0.0, K-slice 0.0, V-slice 7.50; after the fix: 0.00053 / 0.0016 / 7.50). The faithful control is per-slice -- Q/K rows exactly zero at base and nonzero after the fix -- or, for a parameter that sits exclusively upstream of the op (HTSAT's rel_bias_table), a None-to-Some transition, not a nonzero-norm threshold.
